chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a man who gives money to another man and says to him, 'Go to such and such a land and do not exceed it, and buy from it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So if he exceeds it and the money is lost, he is liable (guarantor). And if he buys merchandise and incurs a loss in it, the loss is upon him. And if he profits, the profit is shared between the two of them.'
ai.seo_question: What are the financial liabilities and profit-sharing rules for an agent in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the liability of an agent (wakil) in a specific commercial mandate, establishing that exceeding the designated geographical boundary voids the guarantee, making the agent liable for loss. It further delineates profit-sharing as a joint venture when the agent acts within bounds, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that risk and reward are linked to the scope of authorized agency. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for distinguishing between fixed-fee agency and profit-sharing partnerships in Islamic commerce.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘With regards to the man who gives the goods to the man, so he is saying to him, ‘Go to such and such a land and do not exceed it, and buy from it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So if he were to exceed it and the goods are destroyed, so he would be responsible, however if he were to buy merchandise and incurs a loss in it, so it would be upon him, and if he were to profit, so it would be between the two of them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “About the case of a man who gives a certain amount of asset to another man and tells him to go to so and so city and not beyond it then buy from it goods, abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
’If he goes beyond and the asset is destroyed, he is accountable and if he buys goods and it depreciates it is his responsibility; but if it makes profit it is for both parties.’”
